about.title: Williams Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Williams is a small town, just over 5,000 people gathered where Route 20 meets I-5 in Colusa County. When someone here dies because another person was careless, the loss is felt on E Street and 8th Street, in churches and at kitchen tables. In 2025, public records show 10 injury collisions in Williams, 14 people hurt, and one life lost. One is not a statistic to the family living with the empty chair. California law allows a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children (and in some cases other dependents or heirs) to bring a wrongful death claim. That claim is civil, separate from any criminal charges, and it generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, sooner if a public agency such as Caltrans or the county is involved. LawProactive does not practice law. We listen, then connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so you can focus on your family.

whyChoose.title: Why Williams Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We help you understand who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are connected with will sort out who in your family has the right to bring the claim.

items.title: Deadlines are watched from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks considerably when a government entity is involved. Getting connected early protects that timeline.

items.title: Every recognized loss is accounted for
items.desc: California allows recovery of funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Nothing is promised, but nothing should be overlooked either.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on I-5 near Williams. Does the criminal case have to finish first?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves separately from any criminal charges the Colusa County District Attorney may file. Families often pursue both at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. An attorney can explain how evidence from the crash investigation may still be useful to your civil claim.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there are none, certain other dependents or heirs may qualify. Because the rules are specific, the attorney you are connected with will review your family situation before anything is filed.

items.question: How long do we have, and does it change if a public road or agency was involved?
items.answer: In general, California gives families two years from the date of death to file. If a city, county, or state agency such as Caltrans may share responsibility, a formal claim must be presented much sooner, often within six months. That is one reason it helps to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting for grief to settle.
